title: UNIOSUN MTH 106 - Mathematics for Physical Sciences II

questions.stem:
(a) The radius of a circle is increasing at the rate of 0.1cm/sec. At what rate is the area increasing at the instant when r = 5cm?
(b) What is the order and degree of the differential equations
i. [1+(dy/dx)^2]^(3/2) = k dy/dx
ii. (d^2y/dx^2)^3 + 2x(dy/dx)^7 + xy(d^3y/dx^3)^2 = 0
(c) Evaluate the integrals
i. ∫(tan^-1 x)/(1+x^2) dx
ii. ∫1/(x^2+4x+13) dx
iii. ∫dy/√(1-3y)
questions.explanation:
MODEL ANSWER
(a) A = πr², dA/dt = 2πr(dr/dt) = 2π(5)(0.1) = π cm²/s ≈ 3.14 cm²/s.
(b) i. Squaring to make it polynomial: [1+(y')²]³ = k²(y')², so the order is 1 and the degree is 6 (if the intended form is the curvature equation [1+(y')²]^(3/2) = k·y'', the order is 2 and the degree 2). ii. The highest-order derivative is d³y/dx³, appearing to power 2: order 3, degree 2.
(c) i. u = tan⁻¹x, du = dx/(1+x²): ∫u du = (tan⁻¹x)²/2 + C. ii. x²+4x+13 = (x+2)²+9: (1/3)tan⁻¹((x+2)/3) + C. iii. ∫(1-3y)^(-1/2) dy = -(2/3)√(1-3y) + C.

questions.stem:
(a) Solve the following differential equations
i. y'' - 4y' + 3y = 0
ii. y'' - 5y' + 6y = 0
(b) Obtain the differential equation associated with the primitive y = Ax + A²
(c) Solve by applying separation of variables: (x+1)dy/dx + 1 = 2e^-y
questions.explanation:
MODEL ANSWER
(a) i. m² - 4m + 3 = 0 → m = 1, 3 → y = Ae^x + Be^3x. ii. m² - 5m + 6 = 0 → m = 2, 3 → y = Ae^2x + Be^3x.
(b) Differentiate: y' = A. Substitute in y = Ax + A²: y = y'x + (y')², i.e. (y')² + xy' - y = 0.
(c) (x+1)y' = 2e^-y - 1 → e^y dy/(2 - e^y) = dx/(x+1). Put u = 2 - e^y (du = -e^y dy): -∫du/u = ∫dx/(x+1) → -ln|2-e^y| = ln|x+1| + c → (x+1)(2 - e^y) = k.

questions.stem:
(a) Find the intercepts and horizontal asymptotes of the given function y = (x^2-9)/(x^2+5x+6). Hence sketch the curve.
(b) Find the value of λ for which the differential equation (xy^2 + λx^2y)dx + (x+y)x^2 dy = 0 is exact.
(c) The table below presents the distribution of marks obtained by 1000 students in a statistical test.
Class: 0-9, 10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-79, 80-89, 90-99
Frequency: 20, 41, 98, 149, 192, 197, 152, 97, 44, 10
Compute i. Skewness ii. Kurtosis
questions.explanation:
MODEL ANSWER
(a) Factorise: y = (x-3)(x+3)/((x+2)(x+3)) = (x-3)/(x+2) with a hole at x = -3. x-intercept: (3, 0); y-intercept: (0, -3/2); vertical asymptote x = -2; horizontal asymptote y = 1; removable discontinuity (hole) at (-3, -6).
(b) M = xy² + λx²y, N = x²(x+y) = x³ + x²y. Exactness: ∂M/∂y = 2xy + λx², ∂N/∂x = 3x² + 2xy. Equating: λx² = 3x² → λ = 3.
(c) Using class midpoints xᵢ (4.5, 14.5, …, 94.5) with frequencies fᵢ (n = 1000): mean x̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ/n; central moments m₂ = Σfᵢ(xᵢ-x̄)²/n, m₃ = Σfᵢ(xᵢ-x̄)³/n, m₄ = Σfᵢ(xᵢ-x̄)⁴/n. Skewness β₁ = m₃/m₂^(3/2) (moment measure; Karl Pearson's Sk = (mean - mode)/σ may also be used) and Kurtosis β₂ = m₄/m₂² (β₂ = 3 for a normal distribution).
